formal_name: IB vs RAW Institutional Turf War
description: The structural tension between India's two primary intelligence services — the Intelligence Bureau (IB, domestic) and the Research and Analysis Wing (RAW, external) — that shapes every decision in the Dhurandhar films. Understanding this friction is essential for the oracle because it explains why Hamza operates with the constraints he does, and why KS Bhullar (RAW) and Ajay Sanyal (IB) are not always pulling in the same direction.

ib.mandate: Domestic intelligence — internal security, counter-terrorism inside India, surveillance of foreign intelligence operations on Indian soil
ib.film_representative: Ajay Sanyal (Sanjay Kapoor) — IB Director; Ajit Doval parallel
ib.strengths: Deep penetration of domestic networks; extensive informant base across India; direct line to Home Ministry and PM's Office
ib.weaknesses: No formal overseas operational mandate; cannot legally run assets abroad; dependent on RAW for cross-border intelligence
ib.culture: Bureaucratic conservatism; consensus-driven; wary of high-risk unilateral operations that could cause diplomatic incidents

raw.mandate: External intelligence — foreign intelligence collection, covert operations abroad, counter-ISI, strategic intelligence
raw.director_title: Secretary (Research) — or in common usage, RAW Chief
raw.film_representative: KS Bhullar (Gulshan Grover) — RAW Chief; A.S. Dulat parallel
raw.strengths: Overseas operational capability; direct PM access; ability to run agents in Pakistan, Bangladesh, Afghanistan without Home Ministry oversight
raw.weaknesses: Limited domestic mandate; historically weaker HUMINT in Pakistan compared to IB's informant networks
raw.culture: Operationally aggressive (in tradition); protective of assets; resistant to sharing intelligence that would expose sources/methods

jurisdiction.description: Hamza's Lyari infiltration sits in a grey zone: it is an operation INSIDE Pakistan (RAW's turf) targeting a network that threatens India DOMESTICALLY (IB's turf)
jurisdiction.film_manifestation: KS Bhullar's 'strategic patience' doctrine (don't burn the asset for short-term gains) conflicts with Ajay Sanyal's urgency (26/11 is coming, we need to act now)
jurisdiction.real_parallel: The 2008 26/11 attacks were partly attributed to an IB-RAW intelligence-sharing failure — each had partial information that, if combined, might have enabled a warning

asset_ownership.description: When Hamza (an IB-run operative) develops intelligence that is cross-border in nature, RAW claims operational primacy. IB resists because Hamza is their asset.
asset_ownership.film_tension: Bhullar wants Hamza to stay deep and gather long-term strategic intelligence on ISI's Pakistan-based networks. Sanyal wants to use the intelligence immediately to prevent the next attack.
asset_ownership.real_parallel: A.S. Dulat's 'The Spy Chronicles' explicitly describes this tension — RAW's long-game approach vs IB's immediate threat-mitigation focus

information_hoarding.description: Both agencies historically withheld intelligence from each other to protect sources and maintain institutional leverage
information_hoarding.film_manifestation: Mohammed Aalam's mole suspicion — is the information leak coming from IB's chain or RAW's chain? Neither agency is willing to expose its own potential compromise to the other.
information_hoarding.real_parallel: Multiple post-mortem reports on 26/11 (including the Ram Pradhan Committee) cited poor intelligence sharing between IB, RAW, and state police as a structural failure

operational_philosophy.ib_approach: Hamza should be used to build a comprehensive network map of ISI's Karachi infrastructure — long-term strategic asset
operational_philosophy.raw_approach: Extract Hamza before he is burned; use the intelligence to run discrete operations; don't risk losing the source
operational_philosophy.conflict: In Film 1, both approaches are partially right and partially wrong — Hamza stays too long (nearly burned) but the intelligence proves decisive

political_masters.ib: Home Ministry → typically controlled by different political faction within coalition governments (e.g., 2001-2004: L.K. Advani as Home Minister)
political_masters.raw: PM's office — direct PM oversight means RAW's priorities align with PM's foreign policy
political_masters.film_relevance: Film 2's Naya Bharat mandate represents a PM-level decision to expand IB's mandate beyond domestic boundaries — functionally resolving the turf war by giving Sanyal/IB authority over the cross-border operation

historical_failures_attributed_to_fricti.friction_point: IB had intelligence on Masood Azhar's network; RAW had intelligence on the hijack planning. Neither shared comprehensively with the other or with aviation security.
historical_failures_attributed_to_fricti.outcome: Hijacking succeeded; three terrorists (including Masood Azhar) released

historical_failures_attributed_to_fricti.friction_point: IB-RAW intelligence gap on JeM-LeT coordination; state police not in the loop
historical_failures_attributed_to_fricti.outcome: Attack partially succeeded; 9 security personnel killed

historical_failures_attributed_to_fricti.friction_point: IB had FICN/drug network intelligence; RAW had some Pakistan-side intelligence on LeT's maritime planning; neither had the full picture; state ATS was running separate investigation
historical_failures_attributed_to_fricti.outcome: 166 killed; worst single terrorist attack on Indian soil

film_resolution.film_1: The friction is unresolved — Bhullar's patience doctrine wins; Hamza stays; 26/11 happens anyway
film_resolution.film_2: Ajay Sanyal's Naya Bharat mandate functionally supersedes the friction — IB leads the integrated operation with RAW in a support role; the institutional lesson of 26/11 has been internalised
film_resolution.real_parallel: Post-2014, Ajit Doval as NSA created a new structure where the NSA-PMO axis cut through the IB-RAW turf war — Doval had been IB Director and understood both institutions. The National Intelligence Grid (NATGRID) and Multi-Agency Centre (MAC) were partly designed to force information-sharing.

oracle_implications.hamza_queries: When the oracle analyses what Hamza 'could have done faster,' the IB-RAW friction is a structural bottleneck — not just personal decisions but institutional constraints. CPM analysis should weight IB-RAW approval cycles as task dependencies.
oracle_implications.rizwan_queries: Rizwan operates in the Film 2 context where the friction is partially resolved. His operational freedom is greater — but the oracle should model residual RAW resistance to IB-led cross-border operations as a background risk.
oracle_implications.belief_node: The HMM mole detection should consider whether a leak is institutional (IB-RAW channel) rather than individual — the Mohammed Aalam suspicion may be a false positive masking an institutional leak.
